name: What works
standard: Only interventions graded by the Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide), the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, or a completed Cochrane systematic review. Each entry carries the body's own grade in its own words, including insufficient evidence and recommended against. Each was opened on the body's own page on the date shown. Where none of the three has a finding on an Atlas measure, that measure is left blank on purpose.
review: Partner preview until the data governance board's reviewer (Sarah Fischer, PhD, proposed) signs off; then public.

entries.intervention: Clinician-delivered cessation interventions for adults (behavioral plus FDA-approved medication)
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: USPSTF recommends that clinicians ask all adults about tobacco use, advise them to stop, and provide behavioral interventions and FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for cessation to nonpregnant adults who use tobacco.

entries.intervention: E-cigarettes for tobacco cessation
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: USPSTF concludes the evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of e-cigarettes for tobacco cessation in adults, including pregnant persons, and directs clinicians to cessation interventions with proven effectiveness and established safety.

entries.intervention: Mass-reach health communication campaigns
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends mass-reach health communication interventions based on strong evidence of effectiveness in decreasing tobacco use, increasing cessation and quitline use, and reducing youth initiation.

entries.intervention: Mobile phone text messaging cessation programs
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends mobile phone text messaging interventions for tobacco smoking cessation to increase the number of adults who successfully quit, with a median 4.1 percentage point increase in cessation at six or more months.

entries.intervention: Nicotine replacement therapy
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: The review found high-quality evidence that all licensed forms of nicotine replacement therapy increase the rate of quitting by roughly 50 to 60 percent regardless of setting, with minor site irritation common and serious adverse events rare.

entries.intervention: Raising the unit price of tobacco products
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends interventions that increase the unit price of tobacco products based on strong evidence of effectiveness in reducing tobacco use and youth initiation.

entries.intervention: Reducing out-of-pocket costs for cessation treatment
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends policies and programs to reduce tobacco users' out-of-pocket costs for evidence-based cessation treatments based on strong evidence of effectiveness in increasing the number of tobacco users who quit.

entries.intervention: Smoke-free policies
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends smoke-free policies based on strong evidence that they reduce secondhand smoke exposure, tobacco use, and tobacco-related health events without harming restaurant and bar business activity.

entries.intervention: Tobacco quitlines
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends quitline interventions, particularly proactive quitlines, based on strong evidence of effectiveness in increasing tobacco cessation among clients interested in quitting.

entries.intervention: Varenicline and cytisine (nicotine receptor partial agonists)
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: High-certainty evidence of benefit (varenicline); moderate-certainty evidence of benefit (cytisine)
entries.finding: The review concluded that cytisine and varenicline both help more people to quit smoking than placebo or no medication, with varenicline more than doubling abstinence at six months or longer (RR 2.32) on high-certainty evidence.

entries.intervention: Brief alcohol interventions in primary care
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: The review found moderate-certainty evidence that brief interventions in primary care reduced weekly alcohol consumption at 12 months by about 20 grams per week compared with no or minimal intervention (34 trials, 15,197 participants).

entries.intervention: Dram shop (commercial host) liability
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF found that state dram shop liability laws were associated with reductions in alcohol-related harms, including a median 6.4 percent decrease in alcohol-related motor vehicle deaths.

entries.intervention: Electronic screening and brief intervention (e-SBI)
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends electronic screening and brief intervention to reduce self-reported excessive alcohol consumption and alcohol-related problems among intervention participants.

entries.intervention: Increasing alcohol taxes
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends increasing the unit price of alcohol by raising taxes to reduce excessive alcohol consumption and related harms, with public health effects expected to be proportional to the size of the tax increase.

entries.intervention: Privatization of retail alcohol sales
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends against further privatization of alcohol sales in settings with current government control of retail sales, based on strong evidence that privatization increases per capita alcohol consumption (median 44.4 percent increase in sales of privatized beverages).

entries.intervention: Regulating alcohol outlet density
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends the use of regulatory authority, such as licensing and zoning, to limit alcohol outlet density as a strategy to reduce excessive alcohol consumption and related harms.

entries.intervention: Responsible beverage service training
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF finds insufficient evidence to determine whether responsible beverage service training programs reduce excessive alcohol consumption and related harms at the community level, because most positive studies were small trials at individual establishments under favorable conditions.

entries.intervention: Screening and brief behavioral counseling for unhealthy alcohol use in adults
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.grade: Grade B (adults 18 and older, including pregnant women); I statement for adolescents 12 to 17
entries.finding: USPSTF recommends screening for unhealthy alcohol use in primary care settings in adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women, and providing persons engaged in risky or hazardous drinking with brief behavioral counseling interventions, while finding insufficient evidence for adolescents.

entries.intervention: CBT-based psychotherapy after self-harm in adults
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: The review concluded that psychosocial therapy based on CBT approaches may result in fewer individuals repeating self-harm at longer follow-up time points, although no such effect was found at the post-intervention assessment and the quality of evidence by GRADE criteria was low.

entries.intervention: Collaborative care for depression
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends collaborative care for the management of depressive disorders based on strong evidence of effectiveness in improving depression symptoms, adherence to treatment, response to treatment, and remission and recovery from depression.

entries.intervention: Collaborative care for depression and anxiety
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Significant improvement versus usual care; studies varied in risk of bias (no GRADE rating reported in this 2012 version)
entries.finding: The review concluded that collaborative care is associated with significant improvement in depression and anxiety outcomes compared with usual care in the short, medium and long term (depression SMD -0.34, -0.28 and -0.35), with no significant benefit in the very long term.

entries.intervention: Exercise for depression
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: The review found moderate-quality evidence from 35 trials (1,353 participants) that exercise reduces depression symptoms more than control conditions at the end of treatment (SMD -0.62), an effect the authors interpreted as moderate.

entries.intervention: Home-based depression care management for older adults
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends depression care management at home for older adults with depression based on strong evidence of effectiveness in improving short-term depression outcomes.

entries.intervention: Mental health benefits (parity) legislation
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends mental health benefits legislation, particularly comprehensive parity legislation, based on sufficient evidence of effectiveness in improving financial protection and increasing appropriate utilization of mental health services for people with mental health conditions.

entries.intervention: Multi-tiered trauma-informed school programs
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF finds insufficient evidence to determine whether multi-tiered trauma-informed school programs reduce PTSD symptoms or improve mental health and school-related outcomes, because of gaps in study design despite a median 34 percent reduction in PTSD symptoms in included studies.

entries.intervention: Screening adolescents for depression; screening youth for suicide risk
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.grade: Grade B (major depressive disorder, ages 12 to 18); I statement (depression, age 11 or younger); I statement (suicide risk, children and adolescents)
entries.finding: USPSTF recommends screening for major depressive disorder in adolescents aged 12 to 18 years and concludes evidence is insufficient to assess screening for depression in children 11 or younger or screening for suicide risk in children and adolescents.

entries.intervention: Screening adults for anxiety disorders
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.grade: Grade B (adults 64 or younger, including pregnant and postpartum persons); I statement for adults 65 or older
entries.finding: USPSTF recommends screening for anxiety disorders in adults 64 years or younger, including pregnant and postpartum persons, and finds the evidence insufficient on the balance of benefits and harms of screening adults 65 years or older.

entries.intervention: Screening adults for depression
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: USPSTF recommends screening for depression in the adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons and older adults, with adequate systems in place to ensure accurate diagnosis, effective treatment, and appropriate follow-up.

entries.intervention: Screening adults for suicide risk
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: USPSTF concludes that the current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening for suicide risk in the adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons and older adults.

entries.intervention: Targeted school-based cognitive behavioral therapy programs for at-risk students
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends targeted school-based cognitive behavioral therapy programs to reduce depression and anxiety symptoms among school-aged children and adolescents assessed to be at increased risk, with larger effects when delivered by external mental health professionals than by trained school staff.

entries.intervention: Universal school-based cognitive behavioral therapy programs
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: CPSTF recommends universal school-based cognitive behavioral therapy programs to prevent or reduce depression and anxiety symptoms among school-aged children and adolescents, based on small reductions in symptoms across reviewed studies.

entries.intervention: Interactive telemedicine for chronic disease and mental health care
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: High-certainty evidence (diabetes glucose control); moderate-certainty evidence (heart failure admissions and mortality); mental health outcomes not GRADE-rated
entries.finding: The review found high-certainty evidence that telemedicine improves blood glucose control in diabetes, moderate to high-certainty evidence of similar mortality and widely varying hospital admission effects in heart failure, and no difference between video-delivered and face-to-face therapy in seven mental health and substance use studies.

entries.intervention: Interventions to increase health professionals practicing in rural and underserved areas
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: The review found only one eligible study (an interrupted time series of Taiwan's National Health Insurance scheme) suggesting a small reduction in the inequitable distribution of physicians and dentists, rated very low certainty, so the effect of recruitment and retention interventions remains uncertain.

entries.intervention: Nurses as substitutes for doctors in primary care
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Low-certainty evidence (mortality, quality of life); moderate-certainty evidence (patient satisfaction)
entries.finding: The review found that nurse-led primary care may lead to slightly fewer deaths and slightly higher quality of life (low certainty) and probably slightly higher patient satisfaction (moderate certainty) compared with doctor-led care.

entries.intervention: Adapting shift work schedules (forward or faster rotation, limiting shift length, compressed weeks)
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Very low certainty evidence for most schedule changes; low to moderate certainty for a 16-hour shift limit
entries.finding: Forward and faster rotation may reduce sleepiness during shifts with very uncertain evidence, limiting shifts to 16 hours may increase sleep duration with low certainty evidence, and more high quality studies are needed before firm conclusions can be drawn.

entries.intervention: Drug treatments for shift work sleepiness and sleep disturbance (melatonin, hypnotics, modafinil, armodafinil, caffeine)
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Low quality evidence for melatonin, hypnotics and caffeine; moderate quality evidence for modafinil and armodafinil
entries.finding: Melatonin may lengthen sleep after night shifts and modafinil or armodafinil modestly reduce sleepiness in people with shift work sleep disorder but carry adverse effects, while hypnotics showed no clear benefit and all findings rest on a small number of low to moderate quality trials.

entries.intervention: Listening to music for insomnia in adults
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Moderate certainty evidence for sleep quality; low to very low certainty for other outcomes
entries.finding: Music may be effective for improving subjective sleep quality in adults with symptoms of insomnia, with moderate certainty evidence, while effects on insomnia severity and other sleep outcomes are low to very low certainty.

entries.intervention: Person-directed non-drug interventions for shift workers (bright light, napping, exercise, sleep education)
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Very low to low certainty evidence for most comparisons; one comparison moderate certainty
entries.finding: The evidence is too uncertain to show whether bright light, napping, or other person-directed non-drug interventions reduce sleepiness at work or improve sleep after night shifts, and better-designed trials are needed.

entries.intervention: Screening the general adult population for obstructive sleep apnea
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: The USPSTF concludes that the current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening for obstructive sleep apnea in the general adult population.

entries.intervention: Behavioral counseling on healthy diet and physical activity for adults with cardiovascular risk factors
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: The USPSTF recommends offering or referring adults with cardiovascular disease risk factors to behavioral counseling interventions to promote a healthy diet and physical activity.

entries.intervention: Behavioral counseling on healthy diet and physical activity for adults without cardiovascular risk factors
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians individualize the decision to offer or refer adults without cardiovascular disease risk factors to behavioral counseling interventions to promote a healthy diet and physical activity.

entries.intervention: Built environment approaches combining transportation system interventions with land use and environmental design
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends combined built environment approaches to increase physical activity, based on a systematic review finding that combinations of activity-friendly transportation and land use features were associated with higher transportation-related and recreational physical activity and total walking.

entries.intervention: Community-wide campaigns to increase physical activity
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends community-wide campaigns on the basis of strong evidence of effectiveness in increasing physical activity and improving physical fitness among adults and children.

entries.intervention: Community-wide multi-strategy interventions for increasing physical activity
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Low to high certainty evidence, typically no evidence of benefit
entries.finding: Across 33 studies, the review found typically no evidence of benefit or effect from community-wide interventions on the percentage of people physically active or on energy expenditure, with certainty ranging from low to high depending on the outcome and follow-up.

entries.intervention: Creating or improving access to places for physical activity combined with informational outreach
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends the creation of or enhanced access to places for physical activity combined with informational outreach, based on strong evidence of effectiveness in increasing physical activity and improving physical fitness.

entries.intervention: Individually-adapted health behavior change programs for physical activity
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends individually-adapted health behavior change programs based on strong evidence of effectiveness in increasing physical activity and improving physical fitness among adults and children.

entries.intervention: Physical activity interventions that include activity monitors for adults with overweight or obesity
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends physical activity promotion interventions that include activity monitors based on sufficient evidence of effectiveness in increasing physical activity in adults with overweight or obesity, with gains shown over three months or less and longer-term maintenance unclear.

entries.intervention: Social support interventions in community settings (walking groups, buddy systems)
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends efforts made in community settings to provide social support for increasing physical activity, based on strong evidence of effectiveness in increasing physical activity and improving physical fitness among adults.

entries.intervention: Stand-alone mass media campaigns to increase physical activity
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF finds insufficient evidence to determine the effectiveness of stand-alone mass media campaigns to increase physical activity at the population level, with the 16 included studies showing small and inconsistent changes.

entries.intervention: Combined diet and physical activity promotion programs for people at increased risk of type 2 diabetes
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends combined diet and physical activity promotion programs for people at increased risk of type 2 diabetes to reduce new-onset diabetes, with the 16 studies reporting this outcome showing a median 11 percentage point reduction in people developing diabetes.

entries.intervention: Diabetes management interventions engaging community health workers
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends interventions engaging community health workers for diabetes management, which improved blood sugar control and reduced healthcare use, with mixed results for cardiovascular risk factors and weight.

entries.intervention: Diabetes prevention interventions engaging community health workers
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends interventions engaging community health workers for diabetes prevention, which improved participants' blood sugar control and weight-related outcomes and reduced rates of progression to type 2 diabetes.

entries.intervention: Diet plus physical activity for prevention or delay of type 2 diabetes in people at increased risk
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Moderate quality evidence for diet plus physical activity; very low to low quality evidence for diet alone or physical activity alone
entries.finding: Diet plus physical activity reduces or delays the onset of type 2 diabetes in people with impaired glucose tolerance with moderate quality evidence, while there is no firm evidence that diet alone or physical activity alone changes diabetes risk, and most trials did not measure complications or quality of life.

entries.intervention: Intensive multicomponent behavioral interventions for adults with obesity
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians offer or refer adults with a body mass index of 30 or higher to intensive, multicomponent behavioral interventions; the page notes an update is in progress.

entries.intervention: Screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 with overweight or obesity
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity, and that clinicians offer or refer patients with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions.

entries.intervention: Team-based care for patients with type 2 diabetes
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends team-based care to control type 2 diabetes, which compared with usual care lowered A1c by a mean of 0.5 percent, systolic blood pressure by 5.5 mmHg and LDL cholesterol by 8.0 mg/dL.

entries.intervention: Technology-supported multicomponent coaching or counseling to reduce weight
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends multicomponent interventions that use technology-supported coaching or counseling to help clients lose weight, with all included studies reporting weight loss and a median decrease of 8.1 pounds over a median of six months.

entries.intervention: Worksite programs to improve diet and physical activity and reduce weight
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.grade: Recommended, strong evidence (finding page wording; CPSTF findings index lists it as sufficient evidence)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends worksite programs intended to improve diet and physical activity behaviors based on evidence of effectiveness for reducing weight among employees, with employees in individually randomized trials losing an average of 2.8 pounds relative to controls at 12 months.

entries.intervention: Fruit and vegetable incentive programs for households with lower incomes
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The Task Force found strong evidence that fruit and vegetable incentive programs for lower-income households reduce household food insecurity (median 18 percentage point drop across 7 studies) and increase fruit and vegetable consumption.

entries.intervention: Healthy School Meals for All (universal free school meals)
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The Task Force recommends Healthy School Meals for All to increase student meal participation (median 4.5 percentage point increase across 14 studies) and reduce absenteeism; the review did not measure household food insecurity and lists that as an unanswered question.

entries.intervention: Home-delivered and congregate meal services for older adults
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The Task Force found that home-delivered and congregate meal services for independently living adults age 60 and older reduce malnutrition (15.5 and 9.0 percentage point reductions respectively) and increase the share meeting energy and protein intake recommendations; food insecurity was not measured directly.

entries.intervention: Housing improvements (warmth and energy efficiency, rehousing, area-based renewal)
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: No GRADE certainty rating; authors conclude housing investment that improves warmth can improve health, with unclear effects for area-based programs
entries.finding: Cochrane found that housing improvements that make homes warmer and more comfortable can improve health, with the largest gains when targeted to households with inadequate warmth or chronic respiratory disease, while health effects of area-based renewal that does not target individual need were unclear and evidence on fuel costs was inconsistent.

entries.intervention: Permanent supportive housing with Housing First
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The Task Force found strong evidence that permanent supportive housing with Housing First for people experiencing homelessness who have a disabling condition increases housing stability, decreases homelessness and improves quality of life, with economic benefits exceeding program costs in the United States.

entries.intervention: Tenant-based housing voucher programs
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The Task Force found sufficient evidence that tenant-based housing voucher programs improve housing quality and reduce housing insecurity, homelessness, neighborhood poverty, household poverty and food insecurity (median 7.2 percentage point reduction) for adults, with later gains in education, employment and income for children who moved when young.

entries.intervention: Center-based early childhood education programs
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The Task Force found strong evidence that center-based early childhood education programs for low-income 3 and 4 year olds improve educational outcomes, with a median benefit-to-cost ratio of 3.39 to 1 from projected future earnings gains alone.

entries.intervention: Supported employment for adults with severe mental illness
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: Cochrane found that supported employment and augmented supported employment were the most effective interventions for helping adults with severe mental illness obtain and keep competitive employment (RR 2.72 versus psychiatric care only at long-term follow-up, low quality evidence), with no increase in adverse events.

entries.intervention: Welfare-to-work interventions for lone parents
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Moderate certainty (early employment and income effects); low to moderate certainty (health outcomes); very low to moderate certainty (later follow-up)
entries.finding: Cochrane found that welfare-to-work programs slightly increased lone parents' employment and income at 18 to 48 months with the difference largely gone by 49 to 72 months, had very small effects on parent and child mental and physical health that were unlikely to be substantively important, and most participants remained in poverty.

entries.intervention: Video calls for older people in care settings
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Very low certainty evidence; no clear difference in loneliness versus usual care
entries.finding: Three small studies (201 participants, mostly nursing home residents) found no clear difference in loneliness between video call interventions and usual care at three months, with very low certainty of evidence, and no study reported social isolation.
entries.note: Rapid review CD013632 (Noone et al.). This is the only completed Cochrane review found that grades an intervention directly on loneliness.

entries.intervention: Child safety seat laws mandating use
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends child safety seat laws to increase their use; across nine studies the laws were associated with a median 35 percent drop in fatal injuries, a 17 percent drop in fatal and nonfatal injuries combined, and a 13 percentage point rise in observed seat use.
entries.note: Grade and year from the CPSTF Motor Vehicle Injury findings index.

entries.intervention: Exercise for preventing falls in community dwelling older people
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: Exercise programmes reduce the rate of falls by 23 percent (rate ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83) and the number of people experiencing one or more falls by 15 percent (risk ratio 0.85) in older people living in the community, both rated high certainty.
entries.note: Sherrington et al., CD012424.pub2, published 31 January 2019.

entries.intervention: Exercise interventions to prevent falls in older adults
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: The USPSTF recommends exercise interventions to prevent falls in community dwelling adults 65 years or older who are at increased risk for falls, concluding with moderate certainty that the net benefit is moderate.

entries.intervention: Ignition interlocks for convicted alcohol impaired drivers
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends the use of ignition interlocks for people convicted of alcohol impaired driving, based on evidence that re-arrest rates for alcohol impaired driving fall while the devices are installed.
entries.note: Grade and year from the CPSTF Motor Vehicle Injury findings index.

entries.intervention: Multifactorial and multiple component interventions for preventing falls in community dwelling older people
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.finding: Multifactorial interventions may reduce the rate of falls (rate ratio 0.77, low certainty) but may make little or no difference to the number of people who fall (risk ratio 0.96, low certainty), while multiple component interventions probably reduce both the rate of falls (rate ratio 0.74) and the risk of falling (risk ratio 0.82), both moderate certainty.
entries.note: Hopewell et al., CD012221.pub2, published 23 July 2018.

entries.intervention: Multifactorial interventions to prevent falls in older adults
entries.body: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
entries.finding: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians individualize the decision to offer multifactorial interventions to prevent falls to community dwelling adults 65 years or older at increased risk for falls, concluding that the net benefit is small.
entries.note: Same statement as the exercise recommendation, published June 4, 2024.

entries.intervention: Primary (vs. secondary) safety belt enforcement laws
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends primary safety belt laws over secondary enforcement laws to reduce motor vehicle related injuries and deaths; primary law states showed a median 8 percent drop in fatal injuries and a median 14 percentage point rise in observed belt use.
entries.note: Grade and year from the CPSTF Motor Vehicle Injury findings index.

entries.intervention: Publicized sobriety checkpoint programs
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: The CPSTF recommends publicized sobriety checkpoint programs based on strong evidence of effectiveness in reducing alcohol impaired driving, with U.S. studies showing decreases in alcohol involved crash fatalities and in drivers over the legal blood alcohol limit.
entries.note: Updates and replaces the 2000 finding on sobriety checkpoints.

entries.intervention: Safety belt laws mandating use
entries.body: Community Preventive Services Task Force (The Community Guide)
entries.finding: Based on 33 studies, safety belt use laws were associated with a median 9 percent decrease in fatal injuries, an 8 percent decrease in fatal and nonfatal injuries combined, and a median 33 percentage point increase in observed belt use.
entries.note: Grade and year taken from the CPSTF Motor Vehicle Injury findings index (https://www.thecommunityguide.org/content/task-force-findings-motor-vehicle-injury); the finding page itself shows results but not the grade text.

entries.intervention: Antioxidant vitamin supplements (beta-carotene, vitamin A, vitamin E) for preventing mortality
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Evidence does not support use; beta-carotene and vitamin E seem to increase mortality (low risk of bias trials RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.07)
entries.finding: Across 78 trials, antioxidant supplements did not reduce all-cause mortality and in trials at low risk of bias slightly increased it (RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.07), with the increase linked to beta-carotene and possibly vitamin E, so the authors conclude the evidence does not support antioxidant supplements in the general population or in patients with various diseases.
entries.note: Bjelakovic et al., CD007176.pub2, published 14 March 2012. Title and date confirmed on the Cochrane Library record; conclusions read from Cochrane's own plain language summary at https://www.cochrane.org/CD007176/antioxidant-supplements-for-prevention-of-mortality-in-healthy-participants-and-patients-with-various. This is a recommended against type finding.

entries.intervention: Statins for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease
entries.body: Cochrane
entries.grade: Reduction in all-cause mortality (odds ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.79 to 0.94); no GRADE certainty rating given
entries.finding: In people without a history of cardiovascular disease, statins reduced all-cause mortality (odds ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.79 to 0.94) as well as major vascular events and revascularisations, without excess adverse events.
entries.note: Taylor et al., CD004816.pub5, published 31 January 2013. Title and date confirmed on the Cochrane Library record; the mortality odds ratio was read from Cochrane's own plain language summary at https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD004816_statins-preventing-cardiovascular-disease-people-without-history-cardiovascular-disease because the Library abstract page did not load.

note: Three Cochrane reviews whose evidence comes only from low- and middle-income countries (unconditional cash transfers, community-level food access, supplementary feeding) were left off because they do not describe a Nebraska county.
